title: Moonanum James - UAINE - Plymouth Police Department

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

I request copies of all public records maintained by the Plymouth Police Department and the Town of Plymouth concerning Roland Francis Moonamun James (deceased December 4, 2020; see attached obituary), the United American Indians of New England (UAINE), and annual National Day of Mourning gatherings in Plymouth from January 1, 1997, through December 31, 2020.

1. Subject Identification
- Full Name: Roland Francis Moonamun James (also spelled Roland Francis Moonanum James; commonly known as Moonamun James, Moonanum James, and Roland F. James)
- Date of Birth: March 3, 1950 | Date of Death: December 4, 2020
- Tribal Affiliation: Wampanoag Tribe of Gay Head (Aquinnah)
- Role: Co-Leader, United American Indians of New England (UAINE); Co-organizer and primary speaker, Annual National Day of Mourning on Cole's Hill, Plymouth, Massachusetts

2. Specific Records Requested
Please search all police department operational files, investigative archives, digital evidence systems, and municipal administrative records from January 1, 1997, through December 31, 2020, for records referencing Roland Francis Moonamun James, UAINE, or the National Day of Mourning, including:
- Crowd-Control Operations & Tactical Plans: Operational orders, crowd-management plans, street-closure and traffic-detail directives, mutual-aid requests, command-post logs, and after-action reviews for National Day of Mourning gatherings on Cole's Hill and through downtown Plymouth (including the November 27, 1997 protest and all subsequent annual Thanksgiving Day gatherings through November 26, 2020);
- Intelligence Briefings & Inter-Agency Communications: Pre-event intelligence briefings, threat assessments, roll-call bulletins, and correspondence with the Massachusetts State Police, Commonwealth Fusion Center, FBI, Plymouth County Sheriff's Department, or private/civic event organizers referencing Moonamun James or UAINE;
- Body-Worn Camera, Dashcam & Surveillance Video: All preserved body-worn camera (BWC) footage, cruiser dashboard camera (dashcam) recordings (including archived VHS/DVD cruiser video from 1997–2010 and digital video files from 2011–2020), and municipal/police downtown surveillance camera footage recording National Day of Mourning marches, rallies, or interactions involving Moonamun James;
- 1997 Arrests & 1998 Settlement Compliance Records: Incident reports, arrest logs, use-of-force/oleoresin capsicum (pepper spray) reports, and booking records from November 27, 1997, together with municipal records, Select Board correspondence, and educational-fund/plaque implementation files documenting compliance with the 1998 settlement agreement between the Town of Plymouth and UAINE.

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Nick Estes
